RESOLVED (TC-11 independent review, 2026-09-17; re-verified independently via `git log --follow --diff-filter=A`): this claim was wrong -- the workflow was NOT already active for the full ~18-day window. It was added 2026-09-10 (commit f9cbe210fb), and its weekly Monday-11:00-UTC schedule means at most ONE firing (2026-09-14) was structurally possible before the Sept 1-18 window closed, not 'at least twice.' 2026-09-14 is also the date the mass-disable's own evidence (inventory/disabled_vs_running_anomaly.md) confirms OTHER workflows had their last successful runs, so zero recorded minutes here is fully explained by the file's young age plus the mass-disable, not a defect.

key_findings: Top 3 workflows (content-governance-checks.yml + llms-generation.yml + skill-governance.yml combined) = 75.7% of total minutes (1,131 of 1,494).

llms-generation.yml (259 min, 17.3%) was not previously identified as a top cost driver in the pre-data proxy analysis -- newly surfaced by this real export. It is push(main)-path-filtered only and does not itself deploy anything (its own header comment says aspose.org-workflows regenerates llms output again at deploy time) -- needs investigation in TC-05/TC-06 for whether this private-repo run is a necessary correctness gate or fully duplicated work.

skill-governance.yml's Windows job (223 min) costs more than its own required Linux job (103 min) -- reverses the earlier proxy-based assumption that the Windows leg was narrow/small and could be deferred.

The public-migration-candidate workflows (all the small schedule bots, including the designated canary aspose-com-targets-watch.yml) total roughly 12.6% of usage combined -- confirms migrating them is safe/low-risk but not where cost reduction actually comes from.

This dataset satisfies TC-04's mandatory acceptance criterion (usage/billing figures reconciled against a real org-level source) directly -- there is no separate proxy figure to reconcile against since the real figure was supplied first.
